system_examples: Tesla Trip Planner — verifying whether an electric vehicle can complete a linear highway corridor where each intermediate charging station provides sufficient range to reach at least one subsequent station or the final destination.

LLVM lld linker — validating whether control flow can reach distant program segments through a series of intermediate branch trampolines when instructions have strict hardware limits on forward jump displacement.
Zigbee linear sensor networks — determining whether a telemetry packet can traverse a chain of monitoring nodes where each transmitter has a maximum line-of-sight broadcast distance.
parsed.explanation: The optimal solution uses a greedy single-pass scan that tracks the maximum reachable index, achieving O(n) time and O(1) space compared to the O(2^n) naive recursive approach or an O(n^2) dynamic programming table. While the problem is primarily a classic interview and teaching exercise rather than a standalone production service, the core concept of maintaining a running reachability boundary is essential in practice. It enables lightweight, real-time feasibility checks in streaming and embedded systems without the memory allocation or backtracking overhead of graph search algorithms.
